title: What do you know about our company / product / team?
shortTitle: What do you know about our company / product / team?
keyPoints: Organize research from broad to specific: business, product, technology, recent news, team.
State only things you have actually verified; one wrong fact undermines the whole answer.
Reference a specific technical detail from their engineering blog or job postings.
Turn any knowledge gap into a genuine curiosity question rather than a guess.
Connect the research to why it matters to you personally.
Show structured thinking by moving deliberately through each layer.
Demonstrate that you treated this interview as a priority, not one of many identical applications.

s1_definition.oneliner: Show concrete, organized research : product, business, tech, recent news, and the team's place in it : then connect it to why it matters to you.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Structured layers** – Move from business model to product to technology to recent news to team, showing organized thinking.
- **Accuracy** – Only state verified facts; one wrong claim undermines credibility.
- **Technical depth** – Reference a specific technical choice from their blog or job postings to show real research.
- **Honest gaps** – Turn anything you do not know into a genuine question rather than a guess.
- **Personal connection** – Close by connecting the research to why this company matters to you.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine Priya hiring a financial advisor at National Bank of India. One advisor says "you have an account somewhere, right?" The other says "you run a current account with a property business, you have seasonal rent inflows, and you probably need overdraft protection in the lean months." The second clearly studied her situation. Being the second advisor is what this question rewards.

sections.s6_takeaway:
I have done quite a bit of research, so let me organize it. At the business level, National Bank of India is a retail and corporate bank, and a large part of revenue comes from payments and lending. On the product side, you run a consumer UPI app for everyday payments and a corporate portal for bulk settlements, serving both individuals like Priya and businesses like Rajesh's company.

On technology, from your engineering blog and job postings I understand the backend is Java and Spring with Kafka for event streaming, and it looks like you are moving toward an event-driven model for core banking. In terms of recent direction, you launched instant international remittance not long ago, which tells me you are investing heavily in real-time payment rails. And the team I would be joining owns the fraud detection platform, which sits right in the middle of everything.

I will be honest about one gap: I could not find much public detail on how you handle settlement reconciliation internally, and that is actually something I am genuinely curious to learn, because it is one of the harder parts of a payments system.

The reason I answer this way is that this question is a preparation test, and the right way to pass it is to show organized, accurate research rather than a pile of facts. I move deliberately from business to product to technology to news to team, I only state things I verified, and I turn the one thing I could not find into a genuine question rather than a guess.

Remember one sentence: Organize your research from business to product to technology to team, state only verified facts, and turn any gap into a genuine curiosity question.
